content.overview: The next test or observation should be chosen because it can change the decision. Sampling, identity and containment must remain linked to the consequence of a false negative, false positive or delayed response.

vocabulary.definition: A test or observation selected because its result can change the differential, containment, release or next-action decision.
A sample selected and identified in a way that reasonably supports inference about the target population or decision.
Documented control of sample identity and handling from collection through transfer and result.

sections.title: Ask what decision the test will support
sections.body: Testing should answer a defined question: confirm a suspected agent, exclude a high-consequence pathway, evaluate affected scope or verify recovery. Avoid tests that add data but do not change the decision.

sections.title: Preserve identity and sampling context
sections.body: Plant/lot/location, plant part, collection time, collector, handling, method and result should remain linked. A result with broken identity has weaker decision value.

sections.title: Containment should follow consequence as well as confidence
sections.body: A high-consequence plausible pathway can justify temporary movement restrictions before certainty is achieved, especially where transmission can occur through plant material, tools, water/root pathways or propagation.

workedExamples: If the case question is whether a donor group can be released, a sample from an unrelated room cannot answer that release question even if the laboratory method is excellent.
commonMistakes: Ordering broad testing without a decision question.
Using a negative result from poorly identified material as universal clearance.
Waiting for perfect certainty before applying reversible containment.
content.practicalApplication: For each differential hypothesis, select one next observation or test, define the sample/identity requirements and state how each possible result would change the case.
content.summary: Good diagnostics reduce uncertainty efficiently while preserving identity, safety and decision authority.
